title: Declared and Undone: An Open Pipeline for Finding Self-Reported Unfinished Work in Research Articles, with a Prospective Test and an Exploratory Case Series
content: Research articles often state that part of the reported work was not done and give a reason. We call such statements parked research questions and ask whether they can be found systematically and what obstacles they name. We built an open pipeline — a local language-model sieve followed by an agentic frontier-model reader — and applied it in two phases. In a development phase on 100 open-access works from four fields, the reader returned 432 candidate rows, or 276 distinct declarations; among declarations with a majority class, 71.2% name data that never existed. In a prospective phase on 100 new archaeology works, with gates fixed before the draw, a blind second reading confirmed 85 of 100 sampled reader positives (work-clustered 95% interval 76.2–93.8), and the sieve retained 95 of 104 statements found by cover-to-cover reference reading of 20 works (76.9–96.7). All coders are language models, so these figures measure agreement within a model-based instrument, not validity against human reading; a human validation study is preregistered. Agreement between two model coders on the hit decision was high (Cohen’s kappa 0.812), and agentic reading agreed with the reference more than the same model reading one passage per call (paired difference 0.177, 0.057–0.318). An exploratory series of six reopening attempts, selected by judgement, found no obstacle lifted. The pipeline, registers, protocols and a manifest linking every number to its source are openly deposited.
